today_summary: GCM26 closed the 9/24 session at $4,318, down $57.90 (-1.32%) — a move of exactly 0.99σ against a 1σ daily envelope of $58 — with ATM IV refusing to bid, slipping to 21.42%. The chain stays call-heavy at 227,928 call OI against 87,765 put OI (P/C 0.39), and the $4,500 call wall thickened again to 12,612 contracts, now $182 (3.1σ) overhead. Real flow was on the put side: 6,195 put contracts traded (+94% d/d) and 2,377 contracts of fresh put OI landed in the $4,100–$4,300 ladder, leaving $4,300 (3,562 OI) as the shelf just $18 under spot. Cumulative net GEX reads -411 below spot with the gamma flip up at $4,725, so price sits $407 deep inside short-gamma territory; max pain $5,500 is $1,182 away at 62 DTE and exerts no pull.
five_day_thesis: Five sessions have cost $81.10 (-1.84%, $4,399 → $4,318) in a one-way grind, yet every headline structure metric stayed frozen — put wall $3,500 and call wall $6,000 unchanged all five days, P/C OI ticking only 0.38 → 0.39, max pain drifting just -$25 to $5,500. What did change is where the hedges sit: the $4,100–$4,300 band absorbed +1,919 put contracts over the week, +2,377 of them on 9/24 alone, converting four days of passive decay into an active downside ladder directly beneath spot. Dealer posture deteriorated in lockstep — the ±$200 net GEX slab collapsed 169.7 → 112.8 (-33%), cumulative GEX below spot deepened -337.8 → -411.1, and the gamma flip ratcheted $4,700 → $4,725 even as spot fell, widening the short-gamma gap from $301 to $407, the largest of the window. Volatility never paid for any of it: ATM IV compressed 24.26% → 21.42% (-2.84pp) across a week that delivered a 1.84% drawdown, so realized has been running at implied while premium stayed on offer. The one countervailing bid is upside lottery tickets — $4,850 calls added +1,872 OI for the week (+1,704 on 9/24, on 2,179 contracts traded, the single busiest strike) and $5,000 calls +986 — a barbell against a falling tape rather than a directional vote.
